why: I compared each verifier check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 requires only "exit code is 1 and stdout ... is empty". Check 2 requires `bad config:`, the exact "$d/c.json" as passed, and line 3 and column 3 "in any readable form", which adds no wording rule. Check 3 passes when it prints `OK` and fails if the call returns or the message lacks the path. Check 4 matches its expect line: `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and `{"port":9000}`. Check 5 requires `npm test` to pass at head and at least one test that checks the path to fail against base src/, which is what the expect line says. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": whether line and column depend on Node's message, ENOENT handling, returning {}, `cause`, and the README. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond what its expect line's words require.
